lines.trans: Rookie Producer Baek turns up everywhere! This is the girl I am grooming as the second Cindy—please look after her from now on.
Jinny, go take a seat beside Cindy.
Do not sit down! I want to use this dressing room alone—please find another waiting room for the new rookie.
What is wrong with you? Is Jinny a stranger—she is the second Cindy, practically your alter ego!
Just like older sister Yuna back then? I used to be the second Yuna, and now Yuna is gone—only Cindy remains!
Stop going around calling anyone the second Cindy.
You seem mistaken—the name Cindy does not belong to you! Whether I manufacture a second you or a third you, you have zero rights.
Why? Because you are nothing more than a manufactured image—and the person who made you is me!
I stayed right outside thinking we should rearrange the dressing rooms—let me escort you to another room.

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?

examples.text: 여기가 바로 편집실이다, 앞으로 네가 가장 많은 밤을 새우게 될 곳이지.
examples.trans: This right here is the editing room—the place where you will pull the most all-nighters from now on.
Here the word for 'is the place' is key.

examples.text: 착각하나 본데 신디란 이름은 네 게 아니야! 내가 제2의 널 만들든 제3의 널 만들든 너한텐 권리가 없다는 얘기야.
examples.trans: You seem mistaken—the name Cindy does not belong to you! Whether I manufacture a second you or a third you, you have zero rights.
This point about right is really important.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.
Did you hear about this someone else's?
I was busy today because of someone else's.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children

meanings.en: to go around, to attend, to commute
meanings.note: Indicates regular movement or carrying something around constantly.

examples.trans: I commute to the company.
I carry a bag around with me.

meanings.note: 르-irregular adjective; conjugates as 달라요 in polite present.
In its adnominal form 다른, modifies a following noun to mean 'other' or 'another'.

examples.trans: Do you have any other questions?
Our thoughts are different from each other.

meanings.note: Bound noun referring to a location.

examples.trans: I have no place to go.
I have no place to go. (2)
I want to making right now.
How about trying to making together tomorrow?

examples.text: 근데 그 찰떡이 여기서 땀과 눈물과 피와 수명을 쏟아야 만들어지는 거야.
examples.trans: Except that fine rice cake is only made by pouring your sweat, tears, blood, and lifespan into this room.
This expression comes from 'gets made'.

meanings.note: Auxiliary verb used after -지 to tell someone not to do something. Ending with -고 (말고) gives a brisk, trailing command. RR: malda.

examples.trans: Please do not worry.
Do not be late, and come early.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

부탁하다.gloss: I ask you to look after her

meanings.en: I ask you to look after her

examples.text: 그러니까 잘 부탁해요, 밖에 맛있는 거 많으니까 식사들 하시고.
examples.trans: So please take good care of her—and enjoy the food outside since there is plenty.
This expression comes from 'I ask you to look after her'.

examples.text: 너 왜 그러니? 지니가 남이니? 제2의 신디야, 네 분신 같은 애라고!
examples.trans: What is wrong with you? Is Jinny a stranger—she is the second Cindy, practically your alter ego!
This point about alter ego, double is really important.

examples.text: 자기 노래 두 곡 전에 분장실에서 이쪽으로 스탠바이 시키고,
examples.trans: Two songs before each singer's turn, bring them from the dressing room to stand by right here.
Here the word for 'from the dressing room' is key.

examples.text: 그냥 핸드폰 꺼놓고 인터넷 하루 안 했을 뿐인데 그것만으로도 되게 좋더라고요, 시간도 많이 생기고.
examples.trans: All I did was switch off my phone and stay off the internet for one day, yet that alone felt wonderful and freed up so much time.
This point about merely, yet is really important.

meanings.note: Can refer to a single person or people/a crowd in general without a plural suffix.

examples.trans: There are many people in the cafeteria.
He is a good person.
It really is new compared to what I thought.
Especially today, it is new and nice.

meanings.note: in expressions like 뭔 소리야? ('what are you talking about?')
audible sound made by people or things

examples.trans: Suddenly a strange sound was heard.

examples.text: 말도 안 되는 소리 하지 마.
examples.trans: Don't talk nonsense.

examples.text: 재계약 앞두고 마지막 단물까지 다 빼먹고 자기가 키우고 싶은 신인 키우고 쓸모없어지면 가차 없이 버리는 게 변 대표야.
examples.trans: Ahead of contract renewal, draining every drop of sweetness to launch a favored rookie and mercilessly discarding the star once useless—that is CEO Byun.

examples.text: 앉지 마! 나 이 분장실 혼자 쓰고 싶어요, 새로운 신인은 다른 분장실 찾아봐 주시고요.
examples.trans: Do not sit down! I want to use this dressing room alone—please find another waiting room for the new rookie.

dummy trans 2

meanings.note: Auxiliary adjective attached to a verb stem with -고 (-고 싶다).

examples.trans: I want to go to Korea.
I want to drink a cup of coffee.

meanings.note: Irregular ㅡ-stem verb: 쓰다 + -어 becomes 써.
Commonly used for tools, money, or time.

examples.trans: I write in my diary every night.
I wrote my name on the very first page of the book.

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

examples.text: 아무래도 미래의 의사다 보니까 공부할 것도 많고.
examples.trans: Well, since I am a future doctor, I have a ton of studying to do.
Here the word for 'after all, naturally' is key.
Aw, really!
Oh, what a surprise.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)
Please sit on the chair.
I sat on the floor.
Go forward.
Do well in the future.

meanings.note: Colloquially used to refer to people of the same age or younger.

examples.trans: Kids are running around and playing in the park.
That person has a really good personality.
dummy trans 1
dummy trans 2

Where are you right now?
Did you hear about this older sister, idol?
I was busy today because of older sister, idol.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.
Please sit next to me.
There is a cafe next to the bank.

examples.text: 예전 생각이 나서 그래, 예전에 선생님들 계실 때 생각해 봐.
examples.trans: It just reminds me of the old days—think back to when the veteran actresses were here.
Here the word for 'old days, past' is key.

examples.text: 아무래도 분장실 조율을 해드려야 할 것 같아서요. 제가 다른 곳으로 옮겨드리겠습니다.
examples.trans: I stayed right outside thinking we should rearrange the dressing rooms—let me escort you to another room.
Let us do that (will move you over) right away.

Why were you late today?

meanings.note: demonstrative determiner placed before a noun

examples.text: 이 바닥은 자기 밥그릇은 자기가 챙겨야 돼.
examples.trans: In this industry, you have to look after your own rice bowl.
This book is interesting.
Please write your name here.
What is that puppy's name?

examples.text: 그동안 차갑게만 보이던 내 이미지를 친근하게 바꾸려는 거야.
examples.trans: I am going to change my cold image into something friendly and approachable.

examples.text: 이 신발은 너무 신경 쓴 것 같잖아, 털털한 이미지인데.
examples.trans: These shoes look like I tried too hard when I am going for an easygoing image.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)

meanings.note: Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

examples.trans: Listen closely to what I explain.
I eat Korean food well.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

examples.text: 우리 신디 13살 때부터 내가 키웠는데 처음으로 자기가 하고 싶다고 한 거예요, 이게.
examples.trans: I raised our Cindy since she was thirteen, and this show is the very first thing she ever asked to do herself.
This expression comes from 'raised her, and'.

meanings.note: Hangul spelling of the English abbreviation PD, widely used in Korean broadcasting.

examples.trans: Who is the PD in charge of the new program?

examples.text: 그녀는 예능 피디가 되기 위해 시험을 준비했다.
examples.trans: She prepared for the exam to become a variety PD.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

examples.text: 아무래도 분장실 조율을 해드려야 할 것 같아서요. 제가 다른 곳으로 옮겨드리겠습니다.
